display.purpose: Section/page headings — kept compact by the Operator Heading Rule; no hero-scale headings in normal back-office pages.

label.purpose: Form labels and table headers; set internally by Nuxt UI components.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid Signal Blue action button — the only accent-colored control on most screens.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(0.56 0.17 255); color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 5px; border: none; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.50 0.17 255); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.56 0.17 255); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Neutral outline button for secondary/cancel actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #3d3d40; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid #c4c4ca; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; transition: background 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #f5f5f6; border-color: #8d8d93; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.56 0.17 255); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Subtle-tinted status chip — color is always semantic (primary/success/warning/error), never decorative.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: oklch(0.97 0.02 255); color: oklch(0.46 0.15 255); padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 3px; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat container — border, not shadow, for separation. Used only for genuinely discrete units, not as default page-section wrapping.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #d9d9de; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: #55555a; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card-value { font-family: 'Inter Tight', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; color: #1b1b1d; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field — neutral border at rest, Signal Blue ring on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #ffffff; color: #1b1b1d; border: 1px solid #c4c4ca; border-radius: 5px; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: 'Inter', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; transition: border-color 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(0.56 0.17 255); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px oklch(0.94 0.04 255); outline: none; }

narrative.overview: Aquila PH is instrumentation, not a storefront. Its staff users spend hours a day inside it running liquidations, chasing cartera, and reconciling accounts — the interface's job is to stay out of the way of that work, the way a well-run control room's panels stay legible under sustained, high-volume use rather than trying to impress on first glance. The system reads as precise and confiable (trustworthy): nothing is decorative without functional value, nothing moves without a reason, and the one accent color exists to mean "act here," never to add visual interest. This is deliberately not a generic SaaS-marketing dashboard aesthetic — it aspires to feel dense, correct, auditable, and fast to scan. The product's visual character must also communicate financial rigor and auditability: monetary results are decimal-exact, deterministic, traceable, and reviewable, and the visual language favors explicit states, clear provenance, stable layouts, and unambiguous relationships between inputs, calculations, results, approvals, and audit information.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, spent rarely — everything else is neutral gray doing structural work.
Flat by construction — border/surface-step depth, no dramatic shadows.
Small, consistent radius (3–10px) — reads as engineered, not soft.
Density and legibility outrank whitespace and "breathing room."
Financial correctness and auditability are communicated through clarity and explicit state, not decoration.
Every interactive/status color routes through a semantic token (primary/neutral/success/warning/error) — never a hardcoded hex/oklch in markup.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The brand accent (Signal Blue) is the only accent in the system — no second competing hue.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Color Rule
rules.body: No hex/oklch value is ever hardcoded in component markup — every color reaches the DOM through primary/neutral/success/warning/error.

rules.name: The neutral-* Not gray-* Rule
rules.body: New code uses the neutral-* scale (or Nuxt UI's semantic classes) — never Tailwind's default gray-*.

rules.name: The Two-Font Floor Rule
rules.body: Never use a font outside Inter / Inter Tight, and never drop below text-xs (12px).

rules.name: The Operator Heading Rule
rules.body: Normal back-office surfaces do not use hero-scale or marketing-scale headings; page titles stay compact to preserve room for filters, tables, and forms.

rules.name: The Context Text Rule
rules.body: Text is sized according to its role, not automatically shrunk because it's secondary — contextual/legal text is never reduced below a readable size to save space.

rules.name: The Operational Density Rule
rules.body: Preserve the maximum useful information that can be scanned comfortably. Never increase component height, padding, gaps, or container size merely for a more "airy" appearance — any increase in space needs a functional reason.

rules.name: The Border-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Flat by default — depth comes from a border or a one-step surface-color change, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Contained-Radius Rule
rules.body: Never reach for a radius outside the five-step scale (3/5/6/8/10px), and never a larger radius than the component class calls for.

dos: Do reach for a U* Nuxt UI component before any raw HTML element or custom-built equivalent.
Do drive every color through primary/neutral/success/warning/error — never a literal hex/oklch in markup.
Do keep the accent scarce — most of any screen should read as neutral gray.
Do match radius to the component's class (rounded-sm buttons/fields, rounded-md cards).
Do use <UiTabla> for every table and <UiSelectorBuscable> for every searchable/long select.
Do confirm success with a toast and reserve inline UAlert for errors the user must read.
donts: Don't wrap content in a card unless it is a genuinely discrete, scannable unit — a page section split into 3+ cards where a single table/list would do the same job is the smell to catch.
Don't use section/page padding beyond the scale already in use elsewhere in the app (p-4–p-6, gap-4–gap-6). No p-12+/gap-12+ "hero-style" spacing on operator screens.
Don't use a linear-gradient/radial-gradient background anywhere in the operator surface — zero usages is the bar.
Don't use backdrop-filter: blur(...) or any translucent-panel/glassmorphism effect.
Don't exceed Nuxt UI's own shadow-sm/shadow-md/shadow-lg defaults — no custom box-shadow value anywhere.
Don't add decorative illustration/SVG assets. Icons come only from the Lucide set and only to label a real action or status.
Don't ship a transition/animation that isn't tied to a real state change or that runs longer than ~200ms. No scroll-triggered or entrance animations.
Don't stack an icon next to a label that already says the same thing, and never use an icon-only control without an aria-label.
Don't scale a control above this system's established compact size (~36px control height) for visual emphasis — use color/weight instead of size.
Don't trade away density or operational efficiency for a "cleaner-looking" minimalist layout — this is the Operational Density Rule.
Don't hardcode a hex/oklch color in component markup.
Don't introduce a second accent hue for "variety."
Don't rebuild a component Nuxt UI already provides.
Don't strip built-in focus-visible rings or ARIA behavior with a custom reset.
Don't use a raw <UTable> or <USelectMenu> — use <UiTabla> / <UiSelectorBuscable> instead.
Don't introduce new gray-* Tailwind classes — use neutral-* or Nuxt UI's semantic classes.
